title: Quote model: CRUD API, lifecycle, and accept-to-roll flow
description:
Quote lifecycle management. Quotes are lightweight pricing documents with line items that reference product variants or recipes directly. Accepting a quote rolls recipes into jobs.

Quote statuses: draft → sent → accepted / declined / cancelled

API endpoints:
- POST /api/v1/spaces/:spaceId/quotes (create quote with customer, line items)
- GET /api/v1/spaces/:spaceId/quotes (list, filterable by status)
- GET /api/v1/spaces/:spaceId/quotes/:id (get with line items and cost breakdowns)
- PUT /api/v1/spaces/:spaceId/quotes/:id (update quote details, add/remove lines)
- POST /api/v1/spaces/:spaceId/quotes/:id/lines (add line item)
- PUT /api/v1/spaces/:spaceId/quotes/:id/lines/:lineId (update line)
- DELETE /api/v1/spaces/:spaceId/quotes/:id/lines/:lineId (remove line)
- POST /api/v1/spaces/:spaceId/quotes/:id/send (status → sent)
- POST /api/v1/spaces/:spaceId/quotes/:id/accept (status → accepted, rolls recipes into jobs)
- POST /api/v1/spaces/:spaceId/quotes/:id/decline (status → declined)

Accept flow:
1. Set quote status to accepted, set accepted_at
2. For each quote_line with a recipe (via variant or direct):
   - Roll recipe with line's quantity and variables → creates job
   - Set job status to 'backlog'
   - Store job ID on quote_line (add rolled_job_id to quote_line)
   - Snapshot cost breakdown into quote_line.cost_snapshot via dry-run engine
3. Link jobs back to quote via metadata or FK

Adding/updating lines auto-refreshes the cost_snapshot for that line via the dry-run engine.

CLI:
- nori quote create --customer <id>
- nori quote list [--status draft|sent|accepted]
- nori quote show <id>
- nori quote add-line <quoteId> --variant <variantId> --qty 6
- nori quote add-line <quoteId> --recipe <recipeId> --qty 6 --vars '{...}'
- nori quote send <id>
- nori quote accept <id>
- nori quote decline <id>
acceptance_criteria:
1. QuoteService with Create, List, GetByID, Update, AddLine, UpdateLine, RemoveLine, Send, Accept, Decline
2. Status transitions enforced: draft→sent, draft/sent→accepted, draft/sent→declined, any→cancelled

4. Adding a line with a product_variant resolves recipe_id and recipe_variables from the variant
5. Adding/updating a line auto-computes cost_snapshot via dry-run engine
6. Accept rolls each line's recipe into a job with status 'backlog'
7. Accept stores rolled_job_id on each quote_line
8. Accept sets accepted_at timestamp
9. Jobs created by accept have quote reference in metadata
10. All API endpoints wired and returning correct responses

12. Go handler tests for all endpoints

title: Dry-run cost engine: compute quote costs without creating tasks
description:
Core engine that takes a recipe, quantity, and variables, then computes a full cost breakdown without creating any tasks in the database. This is the heart of quote generation.

Input: recipe_id, recipe_version_id (optional, defaults to current published), quantity, variables (map[string]string)
Output: CostBreakdown struct

The engine must:
1. Load the recipe's published task tree (or specified version)
2. Simulate batch expansion (same logic as RollRecipe but no DB writes)
3. For each simulated task:
   - Evaluate estimated_time_formula with resolved batch_size → estimated seconds
   - Look up station.costs_hour (or space.default_labor_rate fallback) → labor cost
   - Look up task_materials × quantity → material cost per task
4. Aggregate into a breakdown

CostBreakdown:
  total_labor_cost, total_material_cost, total_cost
  tasks: [{title, station, estimated_time_secs, labor_cost, task_count, materials: [{name, qty, unit_cost, line_total}]}]
  materials_summary: [{material_id, name, total_qty, unit, unit_cost, line_total}]

API endpoint:
- POST /api/v1/spaces/:spaceId/recipes/:recipeId/cost-estimate
  body: {quantity, variables, recipe_version_id?}
  returns: CostBreakdown

This should also work for product variants — the quote system will resolve the variant's recipe + variables and call this engine.
acceptance_criteria:
1. CostEngine.ComputeCost(recipeID, quantity, variables) returns CostBreakdown without creating any DB records
2. Batch expansion logic matches RollRecipe behavior (nil batchSize inherits orderQty, explicit batchSize creates multiple tasks)
3. Time formulas evaluated correctly (5m * {{batch_size}} with qty=6 → 1800s for inherited batch, 300s per task for batch_size=1)
4. Labor cost uses station.costs_hour, falls back to space.default_labor_rate, returns null if neither set
5. Material costs computed from task_material.quantity_per_unit × quantity × material.unit_cost
6. materials_summary aggregates across all tasks (if 3 tasks use walnut, sum the quantities)
7. API endpoint returns CostBreakdown as JSON
8. Go unit test: recipe with 3 steps, 2 materials, quantity=6 → verify all cost calculations
9. Go unit test: recipe with mixed batch sizes (nil and explicit) → verify correct task counts and costs
10. Go unit test: recipe with no time formulas or materials → returns zero costs without error
11. Go unit test: station with no costs_hour falls back to space.default_labor_rate
12. Go unit test: no rate set anywhere → labor_cost fields are null, material costs still computed

title: Quoting, Products & Materials Foundation
description:
End-to-end quoting flow: material catalog with costs, products with variants, quote generation via dry-run cost engine, quote lifecycle, and quoted-vs-actual comparison. Enables the demo story: customer wants 15 walnut tables → generate quote with labor + material costs → accept → roll into job → track time → compare quoted vs actual.

Key design decisions:
- Material catalog: lightweight, no on-hand tracking. Name, unit, unit_cost, supplier. Single source of truth for material pricing.
- Task materials: join table linking recipe/job tasks to materials with quantity_per_unit. Scaled by batch during dry run.
- Station costs_hour: labor cost = estimated_time × station rate. Space has default_labor_rate fallback.
- Product + variants: product is what you sell, variant is a configuration (wood + finish). Variant points to a recipe with variable bindings and a customer-facing price.
- Quote: separate table from jobs. Lightweight record with customer, line items (product variant + qty), and a cost_snapshot from the dry-run engine. No task tree created until quote is accepted.
- Dry-run cost engine: evaluates recipe + quantity + variables → labor cost + material cost breakdown without creating tasks.
- Quote acceptance: rolls recipe into job, links job.quote_id back to quote.
- Quoted vs actual: compare quoted cost snapshot against actual time + material usage on the completed job.
- Job statuses: add 'backlog' for confirmed-but-not-started jobs.

title: Time entry engine: start/pause/resume/complete with discrete log entries
description:
Backend service and API for time tracking on job tasks. Each start/pause cycle creates a discrete time_entry record. Completing a task auto-stops any running timer.

Core operations:
- Start: creates a new time_entry with started_at=now, ended_at=nil. Error if a timer is already running on this task.
- Pause: sets ended_at=now on the running entry, computes duration_secs. Error if no timer is running.
- Complete: if timer is running, pause it first (auto-stop). Then complete the task. NO error if already paused — just use existing entries.
- Resume: equivalent to Start (creates new entry). Previous entry stays closed.

Manual entry: allow creating a time_entry with both started_at and ended_at set (for forgotten sessions).
Edit: allow updating started_at, ended_at, duration_secs, notes on any entry.
Delete: allow deleting a time_entry.

Query: list time entries for a task, with total duration computed. Also support querying tasks with zero time entries for manager review.

API endpoints:
- POST /api/v1/spaces/:spaceId/tasks/:taskId/time-entries/start
- POST /api/v1/spaces/:spaceId/tasks/:taskId/time-entries/pause
- POST /api/v1/spaces/:spaceId/tasks/:taskId/time-entries (manual create)
- GET /api/v1/spaces/:spaceId/tasks/:taskId/time-entries (list)
- PUT /api/v1/spaces/:spaceId/tasks/:taskId/time-entries/:id (edit)
- DELETE /api/v1/spaces/:spaceId/tasks/:taskId/time-entries/:id
- GET /api/v1/spaces/:spaceId/tasks/unlogged (tasks with zero time entries)
acceptance_criteria:
1. Start creates a time_entry with started_at=now, ended_at=nil, logged_by=current user
2. Start returns 409 if a timer is already running on the task
3. Pause sets ended_at=now and computes duration_secs on the running entry
4. Pause returns 409 if no timer is running
5. Complete auto-pauses running timer then completes the task — no error if already paused
6. Manual create accepts started_at and ended_at, computes duration_secs
7. Edit allows updating started_at, ended_at, duration_secs, notes
8. Delete removes a time_entry
9. List returns all time entries for a task ordered by started_at, with total_duration_secs
10. Unlogged query returns completed tasks with zero time entries (for manager review)
11. time_entry.logged_by_id is set to the authenticated user
12. Test: start → pause → start → pause creates 2 separate time entries
13. Test: complete while timer running auto-pauses and completes
14. Test: complete while paused succeeds without error
15. Test: manual entry with custom start/end times
16. Test: unlogged query returns only completed tasks with no time entries

title: Recipe time formula: storage, parsing, and evaluation during roll
description:
Support time estimation formulas on recipe tasks that get evaluated when a recipe is rolled into a job.

Formula format:
- Flat time: '=30m' or '=300' (seconds) — always this duration regardless of batch
- Variable formula: '5m * {{batch_size}}' — computed per-task based on rolled batch size
- Setup + variable: '30m + (5m * {{batch_size}})' — fixed setup time plus per-unit processing
- nil — no estimate

Evaluation during roll:
- When RollRecipe creates job tasks, evaluate each source task's formula against the actual batch size of the created job task
- Write result to estimated_time_from_recipe_secs on the job task
- estimated_time_secs stays nil (reserved for user override)
- {{batch_size}} resolves to the job task's final Quantity field

Time string parsing: support 's' (seconds), 'm' (minutes), 'h' (hours). '5m' = 300 seconds.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Recipe tasks can store estimated_time_formula via the existing task update API
2. Formula parser handles: '=30m', '5m * {{batch_size}}', '30m + (5m * {{batch_size}})', plain seconds '300', nil
3. Time string parser converts '5m' to 300, '1h' to 3600, '30s' to 30, '2.5h' to 9000
4. RollRecipe evaluates formula for each task and writes estimated_time_from_recipe_secs
5. For nil batchSize (inherit), {{batch_size}} resolves to the job's orderQty
6. For explicit batchSize, {{batch_size}} resolves to the task's actual Quantity after batch expansion
7. estimated_time_secs is NOT set during roll (reserved for user override)
8. Test: roll recipe with formula '5m * {{batch_size}}', orderQty=6, nil batchSize → estimated_time_from_recipe_secs=1800
9. Test: roll recipe with formula '30m + (5m * {{batch_size}})', batchSize=2, orderQty=7 → 3 tasks at 40m, 1 task at 35m
10. Test: roll recipe with formula '=30m' → estimated_time_from_recipe_secs=1800 regardless of batch
11. Test: roll recipe with nil formula → estimated_time_from_recipe_secs is nil

title: Time Estimation & Tracking Foundation
description:
Adds time estimation formulas to recipe tasks, proper time entry tracking (start/pause/resume with discrete log entries), and CLI parity. This forms the data foundation for future quoting features.

Key design decisions:
- Recipe tasks store an estimated_time_formula (e.g. '5m * {{batch_size}}', '=30m', or nil)
- Rolling a recipe evaluates the formula and writes estimated_time_from_recipe_secs on the job task
- estimated_time_secs on job tasks is nil by default — user override only. Two fields let users compare recipe estimates vs reality.
- Time entries are discrete records (start/end timestamps) per start/pause cycle, not a single accumulated counter
- Time entries have a logged_by user (who recorded it) separate from task assignment
- Completing a task auto-stops any running timer; no error if paused
- CLI can do everything the API can: start, pause, complete, list/edit timesheets

title: Fix batch expansion: nil batchSize should inherit job orderQty
description: When rolling a recipe with orderQty=6, every step gets 6 tasks because expandTaskTree defaults batchSize=1 when BatchSize is nil. The correct behavior: nil batchSize means 'inherit the job's orderQty', so a step with nil batchSize and orderQty=6 should produce 1 task with quantity=6, not 6 tasks with quantity=1. Also, createChildTasks (formula path) doesn't set BatchSize on the task model, so it's always nil even when the formula specifies a batch size.
acceptance_criteria:
1. expandTaskTree treats nil BatchSize as 'inherit orderQty' — ticketCount=1 for nil batchSize steps regardless of orderQty
2. createChildTasks (formula path, ~line 281) sets BatchSize on the created task when the formula step specifies one
3. BatchSize=1 explicitly set on a step means 'one per unit' — ticketCount=orderQty/1=orderQty (this already works)
4. Rolling a recipe with 3 steps (nil, nil, batchSize=1) and orderQty=6 produces: 1 task, 1 task, 6 tasks
5. Existing batch expansion tests updated to cover nil batchSize inheritance
6. New test: roll recipe where no steps have explicit batchSize, verify 1 task per step
close_reason: Fixed nil batchSize to inherit orderQty in both createChildTasks and expandTaskTree. Added BatchSize field to formula-created tasks. Updated and added tests.

title: Roll service: batch expansion + dependency wiring
description:
Extends the roll service to handle batch production (order_qty > 1):

Batch expansion logic (ported from existing pour service):
- Each recipe step has a batch_size (default 1, meaning per-piece)
- ticket_count = order_qty / batch_size (must divide evenly)
- Per-piece steps (ticket_count > 1): create N tasks, one per unit
- Batch steps (ticket_count = 1): create 1 task with Quantity = batch_size

Dependency wiring (ported from existing pour service ~90 lines):
- 1:1 (same ticket count): positional wiring — downstream[i] depends on upstream[i]
- Fan-out (fewer upstream → more downstream): every downstream depends on every upstream
- Fan-in (more upstream → fewer downstream): every downstream depends on every upstream

Title support for batch tasks: {{n}} (1-based piece number), {{batch_count}} (total tickets)

The roll API will accept order_qty parameter. If not provided, defaults to 1 (single unit).

Port the logic from recipe.service.go createChildTasks (lines 210-317) and wireDependencies (lines 378-409), adapting to work with Task rows instead of Formula Step structs.

Depends on: nori-40n.7.7

title: Roll service: clone recipe tree into job (1:1 clone)
description:
Core roll logic — the foundation before batch expansion:

1. Load the published RecipeVersion's root task tree (RootTaskID + all descendants + all TaskDep edges)
2. Deep-clone into a new job:
   - New root task with Type='job', new generated ID (nori-{hex})
   - Recursively clone all children with new hierarchical IDs
   - Clone TaskDep edges mapped to new task IDs
   - Copy station assignments, estimated times
   - Set RecipeID and RecipeVersionID on all cloned tasks (traceability back to source)
3. Accept optional parameters: customer_id, due_date, job title override
4. Return the new job root task

This is a 1:1 structural clone — no batch expansion yet. That's the next issue.

Uses the shared DeepCloneTaskTree utility, with additional logic to:
- Remap Type from 'recipe' to 'job' on root
- Set runtime fields (status=open, created_by, timestamps)
- Strip recipe-only fields or keep them for reference

Depends on: nori-40n.7.5 (needs published recipe versions to exist)

title: Recipe service: publish version (clone-on-publish)
description:
Publishing a recipe version:

1. Deep-clone the draft recipe task tree into a new frozen snapshot:
   - Clone root task (new ID, same fields, Type='recipe')
   - Recursively clone all children with new hierarchical IDs
   - Clone all TaskDep edges between the cloned tasks
   - Clone station assignments, estimated times, batch sizes
2. Set RecipeVersion.RootTaskID to the cloned root's ID
3. Set RecipeVersion.Status = 'published', set PublishedAt
4. Update Recipe.CurrentVersionID to this version
5. Archive previously published version (Status = 'archived')

The draft tree remains editable for future changes. The published tree is a frozen snapshot that roll uses as its source.

Uses the shared DeepCloneTaskTree utility from nori-40n.7.3.

Depends on: nori-40n.7.4

title: Recipe service: create and edit recipe task trees
description:
Service layer for recipe authoring using the task-tree model:

Create recipe:
- Create a Recipe record (identity: name, slug, space, created_by)
- Create a root Task with Type='recipe' as the draft tree
- Create a draft RecipeVersion pointing to the root task (RootTaskID)

Edit recipe (operates on the draft tree):
- Add child step (create child Task under recipe root or under another step)
- Remove step (delete task + cascade children)
- Reorder steps (update DisplayOrder)
- Update step fields (title, description, station, estimated_time_secs, batch_size)
- Add/edit dependencies between steps (TaskDep rows)

Most of this is already handled by the existing TaskService (AddChild, UpdateTask, etc). The recipe service may just be a thin wrapper that enforces recipe-specific rules:
- Can only edit draft versions
- Validates recipe structure (no orphan dependencies, etc.)

title: Recipe-as-Task-Tree, Roll Engine & Quoting Foundation
description:
Replaces the TOML-based recipe system with a relational model where recipes and jobs share the Task table. Recipes are task-tree templates. 'Rolling' a recipe clones the tree into a job with batch expansion. Adds time-to-cost pipeline and job cost aggregation for quoting foundation. Target: investor demo in ~1.5 weeks.

Key architectural decisions:
- Recipes are root Tasks with Type='recipe', children are recipe steps
- RecipeVersion points to a frozen root task tree (RootTaskID) instead of TOML content
- 'Roll' replaces 'pour' — clones recipe tree into job with batch expansion + dependency wiring
- Save-as-recipe: clone a completed job into a recipe template
- Shared UI component for recipe and job task-tree editing
- TOML deprioritized — import/export utility at best, not runtime format
- Formula engine kept as reference, new roll logic replaces it

Phases:
A. Data model foundation (migrations + model updates)
B. Recipe CRUD (task-tree based, service + API)
C. Roll engine (clone + batch expand + dependency wire)
D. Save-as-recipe (job → recipe)
E. Time & cost foundation (TimeEvent auto-creation, labor cost, job cost summary)
F. UI (shared tree editor, recipe list, roll dialog, cost summary)

title: Breadcrumb parent-job link changes URL but doesn't navigate (task page doesn't re-fetch on param change)
description:
When viewing a child task of a job (web/src/routes/spaces/[slug]/[taskId]/+page.svelte), clicking the parent job in the breadcrumb (the <Breadcrumb.Link href="/spaces/{slug}/{parentTask.id}"> at ~line 465) updates the URL but the page does not actually navigate — the displayed task tree stays on the child.

Root cause: the page loads its data in onMount (line ~335), which runs only once per component mount. Navigating from /spaces/{slug}/{childId} to /spaces/{slug}/{parentId} stays on the same [taskId] route, so SvelteKit reuses the mounted component, updates .params.taskId, but onMount never re-runs — tree, selectedTask, deps, parentTask are never re-fetched. The same staleness affects any in-app navigation between task detail pages (relevant to the navigate-on-select beads).

Fix: re-fetch the task tree (and stations/deps/parent) reactively when taskId changes, instead of only in onMount.
design: Move the onMount fetch body into a function keyed on taskId and drive it from a $effect that tracks $page.params.taskId (reset isLoading/tree/selection state on change), or add a SvelteKit load(`+page.ts`) that depends on params.taskId so navigation re-runs it. Ensure derived/panel state (graphPanelTask, neighborhood*, depsLoaded caches) resets on taskId change. Coordinates with nori-zv0.4 (navigate-on-select) which will exercise frequent same-route navigation.
acceptance_criteria: From a child task detail page, clicking the parent job breadcrumb navigates and renders the parent job's tree/detail (not the stale child). Navigating between any two task detail pages refreshes the displayed tree, breadcrumbs, and detail panel. Playwright test asserts: open a child task -> click parent breadcrumb -> page shows the parent job's title/tasks. npx playwright test for the affected spec passes.
close_reason: Task-detail page re-fetches on taskId change instead of only in onMount. Replaced onMount with a taskId-keyed loadTask() driven by a $effect that resets all per-task state (tree/selection/deps/parent/graphPanel/neighborhood/depsMap) and guards against stale in-flight responses via a loadSeq sequence counter. Clicking the parent-job breadcrumb (and any in-app task->task nav) now renders the new task's tree/detail/breadcrumbs. v 6 Chairs complete          (top - final step)
```
  └ Install chair seat
    └ Upholster seats
      └ Cut out upholstery fabric
      ...
```

**Desired:**
```
v Glue lamination            (top - first steps)
  └ True up one edge...
    └ Rip back parallel

        └ Shape chair back
v Rough cut leg stock        (parallel chain)
  └ Joint 1 face on legs
    └ ...
...
v 6 Chairs complete          (bottom - final milestone)
```

Root tasks (no predecessors) at the top. Their downstream dependents nested beneath. Final convergence points and milestones at the bottom. Reading top-to-bottom = following the flow of work.

title: Set up Playwright and write critical smoke tests for frontend flows
description:
Set up Playwright e2e testing infrastructure and write smoke tests that validate critical user flows work end-to-end. This catches the class of bugs where code passes type checking but runtime behavior is broken (e.g., the auth redirect infinite loop in nori-oku).

## Prerequisites
- The Go backend must be running on localhost:8080 (via make dev or manual)
- The SvelteKit dev server must be running on localhost:5173 (npm run dev in web/)
- A seeded admin user must exist (NORI_ADMIN_EMAIL / NORI_ADMIN_PASSWORD)

## Setup

### Install dependencies (in web/)
- @playwright/test
- Run npx playwright install --with-deps chromium (only need one browser for smoke tests)

### Create web/playwright.config.ts
- baseURL: http://localhost:5173
- testDir: ./e2e
- Only chromium project (keep it fast)
- webServer config that starts the SvelteKit dev server (npm run dev) and waits for it
- Set a reasonable timeout (30s per test)
- retries: 0 (smoke tests should be deterministic)

### Add scripts to web/package.json
- "test:e2e": "playwright test"
- "test:e2e:ui": "playwright test --ui" (for interactive debugging)

## Smoke Tests to Write

### e2e/auth.spec.ts — Authentication flows
1. **Unauthenticated redirect**: Navigate to / with no session → should land on /login (not infinite loop). Assert the page is stable (no reload within 2 seconds).
2. **Login success**: Fill in admin credentials → submit → should redirect to / or /flow. Assert the app shell renders (sidebar visible, user name in header).
3. **Logout**: Click logout → should land on /login. Assert page is stable.
4. **Protected route redirect**: Navigate to /flow with no session → should redirect to /login with redirectTo param.

### e2e/navigation.spec.ts — Basic page loads (authenticated)
1. **Flow page loads**: Navigate to /flow → page renders without error, shows content (not a white screen or 500).
2. **Admin page loads**: Navigate to /admin → page renders (admin user should have access).
3. **SOP page loads**: Navigate to /sops → page renders.

### e2e/health.spec.ts — Backend connectivity
1. **API reachable**: Fetch /api/v1/stations (or similar) from the test → should return 200 (not network error).

## Test Helpers

### e2e/helpers/auth.ts
Create a helper function that logs in via the API directly (POST /auth/login) and stores the auth state (cookies) so tests don't need to go through the UI login for every test:

```typescript
async function loginAsAdmin(page: Page) {
  // Could do UI login or API login + set cookies
  // API approach is faster and more reliable
}
```

### e2e/helpers/env.ts
Read test credentials from environment variables:
- NORI_TEST_EMAIL (default: admin@nori.dev or value of NORI_ADMIN_EMAIL)
- NORI_TEST_PASSWORD (default: value of NORI_ADMIN_PASSWORD)

## Environment Variables
Tests need to know the admin credentials. Options:
- Read from docker/.env (where NORI_ADMIN_PASSWORD is set)
- Or set NORI_TEST_EMAIL and NORI_TEST_PASSWORD as env vars when running tests
- Document the approach in the test readme or config

## Quality Gates
These tests ARE the quality gate. Once this is set up, subsequent UI beads should include:
- npm run test:e2e (or a subset) in their acceptance criteria

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] @playwright/test installed and chromium browser available
- [ ] playwright.config.ts exists with sensible defaults
- [ ] package.json has test:e2e and test:e2e:ui scripts
- [ ] Auth smoke tests pass: unauthenticated redirect, login, logout, protected route
- [ ] Navigation smoke tests pass: /flow, /admin, /sops load without errors
- [ ] Health check test passes: backend API is reachable
- [ ] Tests can be run with: cd web && npm run test:e2e
- [ ] Auth helper exists for reusable login across test files
- [ ] npm run check in web/ passes (pre-existing errors in spaces/[id] are acceptable)
- [ ] Tests complete in under 30 seconds total
close_reason: Playwright e2e smoke tests set up with 10 passing tests (auth, navigation, health). Global setup creates dedicated test user. Covers redirect loop regression, login/logout, protected routes, and page loading.

Four columns: **Blocked** | **Ready** | **In Progress** | **Done**

Column mapping:
- Blocked: tasks with status "open" that have unresolved dependencies (not in ready list)
- Ready: tasks returned by GET /tasks/ready
- In Progress: tasks with status "active" or "paused"
- Done: tasks with status "done" or "skipped" (most recent first, maybe capped at 20)

### Task Cards
Each card shows:
- Task title (truncated)
- Hierarchical ID (e.g., nori-abc.1.2) in small monospace
- Priority badge (P0=red, P1=orange, P2=blue, P3=gray)
- Station name badge (if assigned to a station)
- Assignee avatar/initials (if assigned)
- Quantity badge (if quantity > 1)
- Time-ago timestamp for last status change

### Data Fetching
- Ready column: GET /api/v1/tasks/ready (with station/assignee filters from layout)
- Other columns: GET /api/v1/tasks?status=X (with filters from layout)
- Blocked: GET /api/v1/tasks?status=open minus the ready tasks
- Auto-refresh on a 30-second interval (like the existing ready queue)

title: US-006: Task tree endpoint
description:
Add a recursive task tree endpoint that returns a full subtree in one HTTP call, avoiding N+1 recursive fetching from the frontend.

## Context
Currently the frontend fetches children level-by-level: GET /tasks?parentId=X for each node. The flow/[jobId] page does this recursively up to 3 levels deep. For a job with 30+ tasks, this is 10+ sequential requests.

The recipe service already has a collectChildren() method that recursively loads a full task tree. We need to expose similar functionality via HTTP.

## Endpoint to Add

### GET /api/v1/tasks/:id/tree
Returns the task and all descendants as a nested tree.

Response shape:
{
  ...TaskResponse fields,
  children: [
    { ...TaskResponse fields, children: [...] },
    ...
  ]
}

Implementation approach:
1. Load the root task by ID
2. Load ALL tasks where ID starts with the root ID prefix (e.g., WHERE id LIKE 'nori-abc%') — this leverages the hierarchical ID scheme
3. Build the tree in memory by matching parentId relationships
4. Return the nested structure

This is a single SQL query + in-memory tree assembly, O(n) where n = total descendants.

## Also: Add Quantity to TaskResponse DTO
The Task model has a Quantity field (added in y2c.2) but TaskResponseFromModel does not include it. Add it to the response.

title: Graph: newly added serial/parallel node not connected by arrows until refresh
description:
In the graph view, using the keyboard shortcut to add a serial (Alt+S) or parallel (Alt+P) node creates the node and its dependency edges via the API, but the new node renders detached below the existing tree with NO connecting arrows. Root-cause the gap between dep creation and the deps map/layout update and fix so the node appears connected immediately.
design: Likely a race/staleness: refreshGraph re-fetches tasks but the deps for the brand-new node/edges aren't included in the refreshed deps map, or dagre layout runs before deps arrive. Investigate whether the new dependency needs to be merged into depsMap before layout, or whether the parent re-fetch must await the deps load for the new node.

title: Task shown as 'Blocked' even when blocking predecessor is done
description:
On the task detail panel (StatusDropdown), a task displays a derived 'BLOCKED' indicator whenever it has ANY blocker edge, regardless of whether that blocker is resolved. A task whose only predecessor is already 'done' is incorrectly shown as blocked.

Root cause is two-fold:
1. server/internal/handlers/task_dep.handler.go GetDeps -> repositories/task_dep.repository.go GetBlockers returns ALL 'blocks' edges with no status filtering.
2. dtos/task_dep.dto.go TaskDepResponse does not include the blocking task's status, so the frontend cannot tell resolved from unresolved blockers. web TaskDetailPanel.svelte:450 computes isBlocked = deps.blockers.length > 0.

The correct semantics already exist in server/internal/services/ready_work.service.go findDirectlyBlockedTasks, which filters blockers by task.status NOT IN ('done','skipped','cancelled') (terminal statuses). The deps endpoint / DTO / frontend should adopt the same notion of 'unresolved blocker'.

- A task is considered blocked only when it has at least one blocker whose status is NOT terminal (done/skipped/cancelled).
- A task whose every blocker is in a terminal status shows NO 'Blocked' indicator (matches ready_work.service.go semantics).
- Either the deps endpoint filters out resolved blockers, or TaskDepResponse exposes the blocking task's status and the frontend filters on it (decide during impl; document choice).
- The reproduction in the screenshot (Glue Laminate Leg Blanks with a completed predecessor) no longer shows Blocked.
- Tests cover: blocker open -> blocked; blocker done -> not blocked; mixed blockers -> blocked. All tests pass before close.

title: Docker: SvelteKit server hook cannot reach backend (wrong API_BASE_URL)
description:
In Docker Compose, the nori-web container's hooks.server.ts uses VITE_API_URL (http://localhost:8080) for server-to-server calls to the Go backend. Inside the container, localhost refers to the container itself, not the host — so the fetch to /auth/me always fails with a network error, causing every non-public route to redirect to /login regardless of auth state.

## Root Cause
File: web/src/hooks.server.ts, line 4:
  const API_BASE_URL = process.env.VITE_API_URL || 'http://localhost:8080';

VITE_API_URL is the browser-facing URL (localhost:8080 via Docker port mapping). But hooks.server.ts runs server-side inside the nori-web container, where the backend is reachable at http://nori-server:8080 (the Docker service name).

File: docker/docker-compose.dev.yml, line 58:
  VITE_API_URL=http://localhost:8080  (only correct for browser-side)

## Fix
1. hooks.server.ts: Use a separate env var for server-to-server calls:
   const API_BASE_URL = process.env.INTERNAL_API_URL || process.env.VITE_API_URL || 'http://localhost:8080';

2. docker-compose.dev.yml: Add INTERNAL_API_URL to nori-web environment:
   - INTERNAL_API_URL=http://nori-server:8080

This way the browser uses localhost:8080 (host port mapping) and the SvelteKit server hook uses nori-server:8080 (Docker internal DNS).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] hooks.server.ts reads INTERNAL_API_URL with fallback to VITE_API_URL
- [ ] docker-compose.dev.yml sets INTERNAL_API_URL=http://nori-server:8080 on nori-web
- [ ] When running via Docker Compose, authenticated users can access protected pages without being redirected to /login
- [ ] When running locally (npm run dev), behavior is unchanged (falls back to localhost:8080)
close_reason: Verified in Docker: server hook reaches backend via INTERNAL_API_URL (200 with auth cookie, 302 to /login without). auth/health/navigation e2e suites pass (9/9).

Beads 1, 3, 4 can run in parallel.

nori init design: CLI wizard shells out to docker compose (os/exec, no Docker SDK). Writes docker/.env with user config (email, password, account name, JWT secret, NORI_SKIP_PASSWORD_CHANGE=true). Compose file uses ${VAR} references. Polls /health until server up. Then HTTP calls: login -> create space -> create stations -> generate API key (no expiry). Saves API key (not JWT) to ~/.config/nori/credentials. Run from repo root (expects docker/docker-compose.dev.yml).
To refresh bv with current beads data, run: bd export -o .beads/beads.jsonl && bv --db .beads/beads.jsonl
